niche.title: Why a Doctor Invented the Gatling Gun 🩺
niche.description:
Richard Jordan Gatling earned a medical degree from Ohio Medical College in 1850 but never practiced medicine. During the Civil War he noticed that most soldiers were lost to disease rather than gunshots. In 1861 he designed a gun with six barrels turned by one hand crank, patented on November 4, 1862. In 1877 he wrote that a gun letting one man do as much battle duty as a hundred would reduce the need for large armies, and so exposure to battle and disease. The U.S. Army adopted it in 1866 and declared it obsolete in 1911, after 45 years of service.
